newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firm as Eastern arb supports.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firm as Eastern arb supports.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady to firmer on Wednesday, traders said.

High and low sulphur fuel oil prices were firmer with the market fairly well bid and supplies tighter after recent arbitrage offtake to the East. Firmer paper markets and crude futures were also supportive, traders said.
Traders said the spot market was "well bid" but trade was thin with offers of products scarce. One was heard to have moved product out of Greece but details could not be confirmed.
High sulphur fob stems valued around $81.50 with low sulphur liftings around $97.50 a tonne.

Gas oil featured Russian cargoes looking to head eastwards. Two large caroges, one of 45,000 tonnes and the other of 60,000 tonnes which were sold yesterday were both expected to go to Asia. The 45,000 tonne cargo out of Tuapse was sold at fob high quotes +$4.
"The high price reflects it's a good size to arbitrage and it was on a fob basis which is what buyers want," said one trader.
"Stemming east is still viable," said another.
Italian spec gas oil was offered at fob high quotes +$3.5 against an unsuccessful bid of fob high +$3.
Gasoline was fairly balanced with demand seen out of Lebanon, Turkey and Italy, but traders said a cargoes appeared to be available to cover the requirement.
"I think the Med looks pretty steady. It's firmed a bit on the crude but in terms of supply and demand the pictures pretty balanced," said one trader.
Naphtha remained fairly tight but traders said material was available for those who wanted it despite the fact that Egypt and Algeria still appeared to be dry following strong East demand.
